command-code.note: every row of catalog-2026-11-10.csv; list prices are off-peak (17 h/day), weekdays 01-04 and 06-10 UTC double. The plan sells $100 of usage for $10, so a dollar of usage costs ten cents. Page 2026-11-18: the per-model table names 65 models with their monthly credits - $100 on four, $70 on four, down to $10 on one - and this block now carries that table whole, where it used to fall back to the whole $100 pool for any model it did not name. The models the table does not list (Opus 5.5, Fable 5.x) still fall back to it. A processing fee is printed on top of the $10 and the charge carried none. The same catalogue is sold at $1 for $10 of usage, also ten cents a dollar: at a thousand requests a month the cheap tier is enough and costs a tenth. Cross-checked 2026-11-22 against real-api-pricing: its GOAT points cap every model at a $70 shared pool where this block uses the page's $100, so its prices for the shared-pool models read about 43% dearer; nothing moved here on that account. Page 2026-11-28: the GOAT table names 76 models and the block now prices 74 of them. Inkling 2 Mini joins at $15; the older eight the page lists at the standard $20 (Kimi K2.5, Kimi K2.6, GLM-5, GLM-5.1, Qwen 3.6 Max Preview, Qwen 3.7 Flash, MiniMax M2.5, MiniMax M2.7) were in neither the catalogue nor the block and are now in both; and four names the block already carried - Tencent Hy4, Tencent Hy4 Flash, Qwen 4 Max, Inkling 2 Mini - were priced nowhere, because a model's row is its catalogue row, so the catalogue gained those four. The headline allowances did not move: $100 on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, GLM-5.3 Flash and both Ling rows, $70 on GLM-5.2, GLM-5.3, Tencent Hy3 and Qwen 3.8 27B, $60 on DeepSeek V4 Flash and its Fast lane and Kimi K2.7 Code, $50 on LongCat 2.0, $47 on MiniMax M3, $40 on Gemini 3.8 Flash, $33 on the Qwen 3.6 Plus and 3.7 rows, $20 on the standard two-thirds, $15 on Qwen 4 Max, Tencent Hy4 Flash and Inkling 2 Mini, $10 on Claude Sonnet 5.5 and MiMo V2.6 Pro UltraSpeed, and Haiku 5.5's $20. The windows are the same $20 / $50 / $100, and the tiers around GOAT (Go $1, Pro $20, Max $100 and $200, Teams $40, MOAT credits at $10 a month) are recorded, not priced.
command-code.billing_seen: checkout 2026-11-16: subscription payment $10.00, Go monthly, and a $1.00 subscription grant. The page prints '+ processing fee' and the charge carries none.
command-code.allowances_note: docs, 2026-11-16: the $100 is a per-model credit, not a pool - DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and GLM/Ling get 100, the Fast lane 60, GLM-5.3 70, premium 10-20, and Claude Haiku 5.5 exactly 20. Windows: $20 in any 5 hours, $50 in any 7 days.

open-design.note: credit multiplier per model, applied to the price OpenDesign publishes; $10 buys $60 of base Coding Plan credits, so a dollar costs 16.7 cents. The card's $220 / $55 / $18 are the 0.27x (Eco) equivalents of the $60 / $15 / $5 base (60/0.27=222->220, 15/0.27=55.6->55, 5/0.27=18.5->18), not further credits; corrected 2026-11-24 from the maintainer's review of real-api-pricing#257. Go has a 7-day and a 5-hour window. Page 2026-11-18: three more tiers above Go (Plus $20 for 310, Pro $100 for 780, Max $200 for 1,410, with 20, 120 and 300 of Top Model credits and only a 7-day window), MiMo V2.6 Flash and Pro now cost 4x where they cost 1x, and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash carries a 0.25x off-peak promo dated 2026-10-20 18:00 to 2026-10-27 18:00 (UTC+8), now a stale row. The page's Coding Plan table names eleven models and carries no Claude, GPT or GLM-5.3 FlashX row; those three were the console's, not the plan's, and left the block on 2026-11-22: Haiku because the console bills it at x2 against the $1 pay-as-you-go credit beside the plan, GPT-6 Luna and GLM-5.3 FlashX because Go prices neither and has no Top Model credits to draw them from. The block now holds exactly the plan's eleven. Console catalogue 2026-11-18: all fourteen base rates the block carried then matched it, and it prints no cached-write rate on twelve of them, where this block charges input for the same reason. Black Friday 2026 (2026-11-21 18:00 to 2026-12-05 00:00 UTC+8, from the campaign countdown): new subscriptions bought during the campaign get unlimited DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and V4.1 Flash Eco, which then consume no Model Credits; plans bought before the campaign do not, and this one was bought 2026-11-16. Re-checked 2026-11-23: the Cloud model catalogue reprints the same eleven rates (0.30/1.20/0.006 on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, 0.075/0.25/0.015 on GLM-5.3 Flash, and so on), and the console's Plan & balance shows only the 5-hour and 7-day windows plus a pay-as-you-go balance - no per-model counter. The page's "Monthly usage" column is a 60-credit equivalent, in the vendor's own words a "model-specific usage equivalent, not an increase in the shared plan credits": the allowance is one shared $220 pool, and the per-model figures are that pool converted at each multiplier, not caps. Page 2026-11-28: the Coding Plan list is thirteen again and GPT-6 Luna is on it at 4x, at the $15 a month the page gives it on Go, so the block carries eleven. Claude Haiku 5.5 is the one that stays out, and the page is wrong about it: the console bills it at list x2 against the $1 pay-as-you-go credit beside the plan - the maintainer's own route drew that credit to nothing in a session on 2026-11-22 - so there is no plan price for it, only a list price doubled. The pool maths did not move and the page now shows it row by row: its Coding Plan usage table gives DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Eco $220 a month (0,27x of $60), DeepSeek V4.1 Flash $120 (0,5x), the 1x rows $60 and the 4x rows $15, so the $220 on the card is still the Eco-equivalent face value and $60 is still the credit pool. The plan now serves the 1017 build of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and advertises an all-day off-peak week for it; the row keeps the 0,30 / 1,20 the console billed on 2026-11-16, the peak half of that build's official schedule, because nothing since bills the other half. Plus, Pro and Max keep $310 / $780 / $1.410 with $20 / $120 / $300 of Top Model credits and only a 7-day window, and every Top Model stays off Go. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Eco left on 2026-11-28: measured on the Responses shape at 59 t/s against the 85 floor - 2,52 s latency, 100% cache, 100% tools - it was the cheapest point the chart ever drew at 0,00087 a blended million and a row no agent should be run on, so the block carries eleven and the chart refuses any row its own measurement failed. Live probe 2026-11-28 with the plan's own key: /v1/models lists 14 and every Top Model answers 404 model_not_found - Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, MiniMax-M3 - so they are not merely outside the pool, they cannot be called at all with a Go key. glm-5.3-flashx is listed and answers 402 insufficient_balance: it is the one row in the list that wants the wallet. And claude-haiku-5.5 answers 200 but is the only model whose usage carries a `cost` in dollars, where every Coding Plan model - DeepSeek, GPT-6 Luna, MiMo, MiniMax M3.1 - returns no cost at all: a cost field is the fingerprint of being charged per call rather than metered in plan credits, which is what drew the $1 balance to nothing. The eleven rows here are the ones that meter without a cost.

open-kodo.note: Go at $9.9 a month, $99 a year: the plan's own API (openkodo.dev/api/public/plans and /api/public/models, read 2026-11-28) gives it $100 of included usage, $25 in any 5 hours and $50 in any 7, 70.000 requests per 5 hours, and a monthly cap on every model it sells - $100 on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Eco and GLM-5.3, $66 on GLM-5.2, GLM-5.3 Flash, GLM-5.3 FlashX, Kimi K2.7 Code, Qwen3.7 Plus and MiniMax M3, $60 on Hunyuan 4, $50 on Claude Haiku 4.5, $33 on Qwen3.8 Flash, $22 on MiniMax M3.1 Flash, $10 on Claude Fable 5.1 and 5.2, and $17 on the other sixteen. The fee over min($100, cap) prices a million input tokens of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at 0.0149 and a million of Claude Opus 5.5 at 2.33. Three of the site's own figures disagree about how wide the plan is: the pricing page's 'Included models' table names 17 rows because that is the Go-versus-OpenCode comparison, the plan's description still says 'the full 20-model catalog', and the API - which is what the checkout meters - carries 32 chat models, every one of them on Go, which is what the FAQ and the home page say as well. It carried 40 this morning: the plan retired eight Claude rows on 2026-11-28 - fable 5.1, haiku 4.5, opus 4.6, 4.7, 4.8 and 5, sonnet 4.6 and 5 - leaving fable 5.2, opus 5.5, sonnet 5.5 and haiku 5.5 of that family. Nine of the thirty-two stay out of this table under the 2026-11-24 rule, because their price rises past a context threshold and a one-price table cannot hold that: Claude Haiku 5.5 (>100K, x5) and the eight GPT rows (gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-6-sol, gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6.1-terra, gpt-6.2-sol, gpt-6-astra and gpt-6.2-astra; >272K, input x2 and output x1.5). The 31 carried rows are the API's own rates, cache read included and cache write where the API prices one - the Claude rows; a zero there is left as no separate write charge. DeepSeek bills peak hours and the API's row carries both halves, so its three models draw two points each, as they do on Command Code and OpenCode. Unmeasured: no row in models.csv and nothing admitted, so the chart carries these points with no gate behind them. A first Google or GitHub sign-in carries $10 of welcome usage at $2 per five hours and an invite code makes the first month $4.9; neither is in the price. Pro is $19.9 for double of all of it, and is recorded, not priced.
open-kodo.billing_seen: nothing charged and no console read: the block is the plan's own public API, read 2026-11-28, which is what its checkout meters

opencode.note: OpenCode Go, $10 a month: one allowance per model instead of one pool; the month resets with the paid period, the 5-hour cap is 20% of a model's monthly allowance, the week 50%, and Extra Usage spends the console balance at the Models prices. The rates are the Go endpoint's own, as its models endpoint reported them on 2026-11-22: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 0.15/0.003/0.6 and V4 Pro 0.66/0.022/1.98, both x2 on weekdays 01-04 and 06-10 UTC (two points, like Command Code's), and the rest as listed. Black Friday's 60% off is on the Models product (GLM-5.3 1.40 -> 0.56, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 0.30 -> 0.12), not on the Go allowance rates, so it is not in this block. GLM-5.3's $500 is the raised limit good through 2026-11-22 (standard $200 per real-api-pricing, Go Plus $1,000); GLM-5.2 is no longer in the Go endpoint but keeps its hidden console row at $60. Gemini 4 Argon's 50% discount runs through 2026-11-30 and the endpoint doubles it from 2026-12-01. Cache write is the published rate where the plan prints one, and the input rate where it prints '-' (a write is then billed as input); the same rule is in the OpenDesign block. Context-length overrides above the base tier (Grok 4.7 >200k, MiniMax M3 >512k, Haiku 5.5 >100k, Qwen3.7 Plus >256k, the Lunas >272k) are not modelled, and on 2026-11-24 the rows carrying them left the block (six of the seven ids; the decision variant was never carried here): a model whose price changes with context has no single price to compare, so it does not belong in a one-price table. Qwen4 Max and Hy4 are priced from the OpenDesign console catalogue of 2026-11-18; the free models stay out. Endpoint 2026-11-28: Kimi K3.1 Pro's allowance quadrupled from $15 to $60 for the same $10, so its blended million falls from 0,196 to 0,049 and it is the cheapest row above Terminal-Bench 57 on the chart; longcat-2.0 became longcat-2.5 at the same rates and the same $60, and its cache write is the 0 the endpoint prints, not the input rate; GLM-5.3's Go Plus allowance is $400 where this note said $1.000. The roster is 32 chat models, and every new one prices more past a context threshold - grok-4.7 (>200k, x2), gpt-5.6-luna and gpt-6-luna (>272k, input x2 / output x1,5), claude-haiku-5-5 (>100k, x5), minimax-m3 (>512k, x2), qwen3.7-plus (>256k, x3) - so the 2026-11-24 rule keeps all six out, as it kept their predecessors out; the free rows (beam-free, iceman-contributor-free, hy4-flash-free, hungerg-free), the decision models and the embeddings were never in. Go Plus ($40) and Go Teams ($20 a member, two minimum) are recorded, not priced: this block is Go.
